name: DataWarrior
description: HTTPS, but 'verification' is an MD5 supplied by the same server as the jar; auto-loaded via URLClassLoader every launch, Automatic mode skips confirmation.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: DataWarrior’s updater compares update JARs with MD5 values supplied by its metadata. Its plugin channel is separate; these observations do not establish independent publisher authentication or every automatic-update setting.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study checkout; the server response and release process were not independently verified, and the source does not show an independent signature or pinned-key control in this path.

original_evidence.text: | DataWarrior | https://github.com/thsa/datawarrior | 772596aa7 (2026-08-20) | Y | Y-by-default-mode-"Ask" (auto-checks + prompts every startup, `getPostInstallInfoAndHandleUpdates`); a user-selectable "Automatic" preference (`PREFERENCES_UPDATE_MODE_AUTO`) skips the prompt and downloads+installs-on-next-launch unattended | **Y** — `downloadJarFile()` fetches a full replacement `datawarrior_vXX.XX.XX.jar`; `DataWarriorLauncher` auto-loads and executes the newest one on **every subsequent launch**. The identical mechanism is reused for a "trusted plugins" channel (content-as-code side channel, same flaw) | https (`URL1="https://dwversion.openmolecules.org"`, `URL2="https://dwversion.datawarrior.org"`, `DEFAULT_UPDATE_URL="https://openmolecules.org/datawarrior/update"`); no TLS-bypass code found; the per-update `sourceURL` is taken verbatim from the HTTPS-fetched server response with no re-validation | N (plain Java `Properties` key/value response, no signature) | **hash-from-same-endpoint only** — MD5 (`PROPERTY_AUTO_UPDATE_MD5SUM`) is supplied by the very same HTTPS response that supplies the download URL; no independent/pinned signature | server-supplied/unpinned (the MD5 comes from the same origin being trusted — endpoint compromise defeats it) | `src/com/actelion/research/datawarrior/help/DEUpdateHandler.java:55-58` (server URLs), `:123-170` (background thread runs every launch), `:264-329` (`handleUpdate`, Ask vs Automatic mode), `:331-446` (`downloadJarFile`, MD5-only check at `:406-416`), `:448-506` (`handleTrustesPlugins` — same MD5-from-server pattern for plugin jars), `src/org/openmolecules/datawarrior/launcher/DataWarriorLauncher.java:43-54` (picks newest downloaded jar), `:85-94` (`URLClassLoader` loads it and invokes `main()` on every launch, no further check) |
